item.content:encoded:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping industries, governments, and societies worldwide. As AI systems become increasingly powerful, the need for skilled professionals capable of developing effective governance frameworks, safety policies, and risk mitigation strategies has never been greater. To help address this growing global challenge, Arcadia Impact has opened applications for its AI Governance Taskforce Autumn 2026 Cohort, a prestigious research programme designed for experienced professionals who want to transition into frontier AI governance.

This highly selective programme offers participants an opportunity to conduct policy-relevant AI governance research alongside internationally recognized experts while maintaining their current professional commitments. Running over 12 weeks on a part-time basis, the programme is fully remote and welcomes applicants from around the world.

Although voluntary and unpaid, the fellowship provides invaluable exposure, professional networking opportunities, practical research experience, and a proven pathway into careers focused on AI governance, AI safety, and policy development.

About the Arcadia Impact AI Governance Taskforce

The AI Governance Taskforce is a specialized research programme that supports experienced professionals seeking to transition into careers focused on reducing catastrophic and systemic risks associated with transformative artificial intelligence.

Unlike many AI education programmes that focus on technical development or AI ethics generally, the AI Governance Taskforce specifically concentrates on frontier AI governance. Participants work on policy-focused research designed to improve governance systems capable of addressing advanced AI risks before they become major global threats.

The programme enables professionals from diverse disciplines to apply their existing expertise to one of the world’s fastest-growing policy areas while receiving mentorship from leaders in AI governance and safety.

Why This Programme Matters

As governments, international organizations, and technology companies race to regulate increasingly advanced AI systems, there is a significant global shortage of professionals who understand both public policy and frontier AI governance.

Arcadia Impact created the AI Governance Taskforce to bridge this gap by providing professionals with:

  • Practical research experience
  • Exposure to real-world AI governance challenges
  • High-level mentorship
  • Collaborative policy development experience
  • Professional networks within the AI safety community

Participants leave the programme with stronger credentials that position them for future opportunities in AI governance, research, public policy, and international organizations.

Programme Overview

The Autumn 2026 cohort has been carefully structured to accommodate working professionals.

Programme Details

  • Programme Duration: 12 weeks
  • Programme Dates: 12 October 2026 – 15 January 2027
  • Year-End Break: Two-week holiday break between 18 December 2026 and 4 January 2027
  • Commitment: Approximately 8 hours per week
  • Delivery Mode: Fully remote
  • Location: Global
  • Programme Type: Voluntary and unpaid
  • Available Positions: Approximately 20 Research Associate places

Participants can continue with their existing careers while contributing to meaningful AI governance research.

What Participants Will Do

Research Associates become members of multidisciplinary research teams composed of four individuals.

Each team works closely with:

  • A dedicated Research Team Leader
  • A leading AI governance expert
  • Other experienced professionals from diverse disciplines

Together, they investigate pressing AI governance questions and produce policy-oriented research intended to influence real-world decision-making.

Typical research outputs include:

  • Academic-style preprint papers
  • Policy briefs
  • Government policy memoranda
  • Research articles
  • Stakeholder reports

These publications are designed to address challenges surrounding advanced AI governance and catastrophic AI risks.

Learn from World-Leading AI Governance Experts

Participants receive direct guidance from senior practitioners working across some of the world’s most respected AI safety and governance organizations.

Expert partners have included professionals affiliated with:

  • UK AI Security Institute (AISI)
  • Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI)
  • AI Incident Database (AIID)
  • MIT AI Risk Initiative (AIRI)
  • Centre for Long-Term Resilience (CLTR)
  • SaferAI
  • The Future Society
  • Future of Life Institute (FLI)
  • Leading universities and academic institutions

Research Team Leaders work alongside these experts to ensure projects remain academically rigorous and policy relevant.

Areas of Research

Projects typically focus on governance challenges surrounding frontier AI systems.

Examples include:

  • AI incident monitoring
  • AI governance frameworks
  • AI safety cases
  • International AI policy
  • Frontier AI regulation
  • AI risk management
  • Open-source intelligence for AI governance
  • Dangerous capability thresholds
  • AI accountability mechanisms
  • Loss-of-control scenarios
  • International governance infrastructure

Research themes evolve with emerging developments in AI governance.

Outstanding Career Outcomes for Alumni

One of the strongest features of the AI Governance Taskforce is its exceptional alumni network.

Graduates have progressed into positions at organizations including:

  • Google DeepMind
  • SaferAI
  • ControlAI
  • Pour Demain
  • Oxford Martin AI Governance Initiative
  • MIT AI Risk Initiative
  • Centre for Long-Term Resilience
  • The Future Society
  • GovAI
  • IAPS
  • Future Impact Group

Many alumni have also:

  • Secured research management positions
  • Joined international AI governance fellowships
  • Collaborated with renowned AI researcher Yoshua Bengio
  • Started independent AI governance initiatives
  • Returned to the Taskforce as Research Team Leaders

These achievements demonstrate the programme’s effectiveness as a launchpad for careers in frontier AI governance.

International Recognition of Research

Research produced through the Taskforce has received significant international recognition.

Achievements include:

  • Acceptance at the International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML) Technical AI Governance Workshop
  • Best Paper Award recognition
  • Co-authorship opportunities with expert partners
  • Features in Time Magazine
  • Coverage in the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists
  • Publication in the AI Policy Bulletin

These accomplishments reflect the quality and impact of the programme’s research outputs.

Who Should Apply?

Arcadia Impact is seeking motivated professionals who have already begun transitioning toward careers in frontier AI governance.

Applicants should demonstrate genuine commitment rather than simply exploring the field.

Professionals from a wide variety of disciplines are encouraged to apply, including:

  • Law
  • Public Policy
  • Economics
  • Political Science
  • International Relations
  • Engineering
  • Machine Learning
  • Software Engineering
  • Systems Engineering
  • Mechanical Engineering
  • Safety Engineering
  • Computer Science
  • Philosophy
  • Social Sciences
  • Humanities
  • Management

Applicants do not need to possess deep technical AI expertise.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants should be able to:

  • Commit approximately eight hours per week throughout the programme.
  • Work effectively within a structured remote research team.
  • Demonstrate commitment to reducing catastrophic risks from frontier AI.
  • Show evidence of progressing toward a career in AI governance.
  • Communicate clearly through writing and research.
  • Exercise sound judgement when evaluating AI governance challenges.
  • Work independently with minimal supervision.

Arcadia Impact encourages applications even from candidates who meet only part of the preferred profile.

What the Selection Committee Looks For

Applications are assessed using several criteria, including:

1. Motivation

Candidates should demonstrate a clear commitment to transitioning into frontier AI governance.

2. Awareness of the AI Landscape

Applicants should understand:

  • Frontier AI capabilities
  • Emerging AI risks
  • Key organizations
  • Existing governance initiatives

3. Transferable Expertise

Professional knowledge from previous careers should be applicable to AI governance research.

4. Research Skills

Strong reasoning, writing, analytical thinking, and policy research skills are highly valued.

5. Independent Initiative

Candidates should show evidence of creating opportunities independently and pursuing meaningful work without needing formal structures.

Application Process

The Autumn 2026 selection process consists of four stages.

Stage One – General Application

Applicants submit:

  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Short written responses

No writing sample is required.

Stage Two – Project Application

Shortlisted candidates receive:

  • Project briefs
  • A short written task related to their preferred project

Stage Three – Interview

Successful applicants participate in an online interview where they discuss:

  • Motivation
  • Experience
  • Research interests
  • Career goals

Stage Four – Offers

Selected candidates receive offers to join a specific research team.

Approximately 20 Research Associate positions will be available.

Important Dates

Applicants should carefully note the following timeline:

Activity Date
Applications Open 5 August 2026
General Application Deadline 31 August 2026 (Anywhere on Earth)
Stage Two Invitations By 7 September 2026
Project Applications Due 13 September 2026
Interview Invitations 21 September 2026
Interviews Late September 2026
Offers Issued Week commencing 5 October 2026
Programme Begins 12 October 2026
Programme Ends 15 January 2027

Why You Should Apply

Although the programme is unpaid, participants receive benefits that can significantly accelerate careers in AI governance.

These include:

  • Working directly with internationally recognized AI governance experts
  • Building a strong professional network
  • Producing publishable policy research
  • Strengthening research credentials
  • Gaining exposure to real-world AI governance challenges
  • Improving opportunities for future fellowships and employment
  • Collaborating with professionals from multiple disciplines
  • Contributing to research that influences AI policy discussions worldwide

For professionals committed to shaping the future of AI governance, this represents an exceptional learning and career development opportunity.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit their application through the official Arcadia Impact application portal before the deadline.

Applicants with questions about the programme may contact:

Ben R Smith
Taskforce Lead
Email: ben [at] arcadiaimpact [dot] org

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

Applications close at 23:59 Anywhere on Earth (AoE) on Monday, 31 August 2026 (12:59 BST on Tuesday, 1 September 2026).

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications well before the deadline due to the competitive selection process.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Arcadia Impact AI Governance Taskforce Autumn 2026.

Conclusion

The Arcadia Impact AI Governance Taskforce Autumn 2026 Cohort offers an outstanding opportunity for experienced professionals who want to transition into one of the world’s most important emerging fields. Through expert mentorship, collaborative research, international networking, and hands-on policy development, participants gain the experience and credibility needed to contribute meaningfully to frontier AI governance.

Whether your background is in law, engineering, public policy, economics, philosophy, political science, or another discipline, this programme provides a structured pathway into AI governance while allowing you to continue your current professional commitments. Given the programme’s strong alumni outcomes and international recognition, professionals interested in shaping the future governance of transformative AI should strongly consider applying.

For more global fellowship opportunities visit OFY HERE

item.content:encoded:
Are you interested in climate action, sustainability, and achieving a net-zero future? The UN SDG:Learn Net Zero Learning Pathway offers a free opportunity for learners worldwide to develop a comprehensive understanding of net-zero emissions, climate science, and science-based targets.

Developed through collaboration with leading United Nations partners, this self-paced learning pathway helps individuals, professionals, students, policymakers, and organizations understand how to align climate actions with global goals and contribute to a more sustainable future.

The pathway combines three specialized courses that guide learners from foundational concepts to practical implementation of net-zero strategies.

 

About the Net Zero Learning Pathway

The Net Zero Learning Pathway introduces participants to the science behind climate change, the importance of achieving net-zero emissions, and the frameworks used by organizations worldwide to set and achieve climate goals.

Through a structured learning journey, participants will:

• Understand the fundamentals of net-zero emissions.

• Learn why climate action is critical for sustainable development.

• Explore practical approaches to reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

• Understand science-based target methodologies.

• Learn how organizations align climate commitments with the 1.5°C pathway.

• Gain knowledge of internationally recognized net-zero standards.

The pathway is completely online and self-paced, allowing learners to study at their convenience.

 

What You Will Learn

The learning pathway is divided into three modules that progressively build climate knowledge and practical skills.

Module 1: Understanding Net Zero

Course 1: The Net-Zero Standard

Provider:  United Nations Global Compact (UNGC)

This course introduces learners to the concept of net-zero emissions and explains why reaching net zero is essential for addressing climate change.

Participants will explore:

• Climate science fundamentals.

• The role of net-zero strategies in limiting global warming.

• Key concepts and terminology related to net-zero commitments.

• Practical actions that organizations and individuals can take to reduce emissions.

This course provides the foundation needed to understand broader climate action frameworks.

Module 2: Science-Based Targets for Net Zero

Course 2: Net Zero 101: What, Why and How

Provider:United Nations University (UNU)

This introductory course examines the importance of net-zero commitments and provides practical guidance on how organizations can contribute to global climate goals.

Participants will learn:

• What net zero means in practice.

• Why net-zero commitments matter.

• How emissions reductions contribute to climate mitigation.

• Key approaches for implementing climate strategies.

• The relationship between sustainability and long-term resilience.

The course is ideal for individuals seeking a broader understanding of climate solutions and net-zero implementation.

Module 3: The Net-Zero Standard in Practice

Course 3: Setting Science-Based Targets to Achieve Net-Zero

Provider: United Nations Global Compact (UNGC)

This advanced course focuses on helping organizations establish science-based targets that align with global climate objectives.

Participants will explore:

• Science-based target methodologies.

• Setting near-term and long-term emissions reduction goals.

• Aligning organizational targets with the 1.5°C climate pathway.

• Best practices for implementing the Net-Zero Standard.

• Strategies for measuring and tracking climate progress.

This course is particularly valuable for sustainability professionals, business leaders, policymakers, and organizations seeking to strengthen their climate commitments.

 

Who Should Enroll?

The Net Zero Learning Pathway is suitable for:

• Students and young professionals.

• Climate and sustainability advocates.

• Environmental practitioners.

• Corporate sustainability teams.

• Government officials and policymakers.

• NGO professionals.

• Researchers and academics.

• Anyone interested in climate action and sustainable development.

No prior experience is required to begin the pathway.

 

Benefits of the Learning Pathway

Participants will benefit from:

• Free access to high-quality United Nations learning resources.

• Flexible self-paced learning.

• Expert insights from leading global institutions.

• Practical knowledge on climate action and net-zero implementation.

• Skills relevant to sustainability and environmental careers.

• Increased understanding of science-based climate targets.

• Enhanced capacity to contribute to organizational and community climate initiatives.

 

Why Net Zero Matters

Net-zero emissions have become a central goal in global efforts to combat climate change. Governments, businesses, institutions, and communities worldwide are adopting net-zero commitments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and limit global warming.

Understanding how net-zero frameworks operate and how science-based targets are established is increasingly important for professionals working in sustainability, environmental management, policy development, and corporate responsibility.

This learning pathway provides a valuable opportunity to gain these critical skills at no cost.

 

Conclusion

The UN SDG:Learn Net Zero Learning Pathway offers a comprehensive and accessible introduction to climate action, net-zero standards, and science-based targets. Through three expertly designed courses from the United Nations Global Compact and United Nations University, learners can build the knowledge and practical skills needed to support a sustainable, low-carbon future.

Whether you are a student, sustainability professional, policymaker, or simply passionate about climate action, this free learning opportunity can help you better understand the pathways toward achieving global climate goals and creating meaningful environmental impact.

Discover more opportunities like this HERE.

item.content:encoded:
Germany has long been recognized as one of the world’s leading destinations for higher education, research, and academic innovation. Every year, thousands of international students choose German universities and research institutions because of their world-class education, cutting-edge research opportunities, affordable study options, and vibrant multicultural environment.

To encourage more students to explore these opportunities, the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) has officially opened applications for the DAAD Young Ambassadors 2027 Programme. This unique initiative is designed for enthusiastic alumni and current students who have studied or conducted research in Germany and are passionate about sharing their experiences with others.

The programme offers participants an opportunity to become official representatives of German higher education in their home countries by promoting study and research opportunities through presentations, outreach activities, educational events, and student engagement initiatives.

If your time in Germany transformed your academic or professional journey and you are eager to motivate others to pursue similar opportunities, this programme provides the perfect platform to make an impact.

What is the DAAD Young Ambassadors Programme?

The DAAD Young Ambassadors Programme is an outreach initiative organized by the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD). The programme brings together former and current international students and researchers who have firsthand experience studying in Germany.

Rather than serving as a traditional scholarship, the programme focuses on educational outreach and peer-to-peer engagement. Selected ambassadors use their personal experiences to educate prospective students about studying and conducting research in Germany.

Young Ambassadors become trusted voices who can answer questions, share practical insights, and encourage talented students to consider Germany as a destination for higher education.

Through presentations, educational fairs, seminars, university events, and other awareness activities, ambassadors help bridge the information gap between prospective applicants and German institutions.

Why Germany?

Germany continues to rank among the world’s most attractive study destinations due to numerous academic and professional advantages.

Some of these include:

  • Internationally recognized universities
  • High-quality education
  • Strong research infrastructure
  • Numerous English-taught programmes
  • Affordable or tuition-free education at many public universities
  • Excellent career opportunities
  • Strong links between academia and industry
  • Rich cultural diversity
  • Global networking opportunities

The Young Ambassadors Programme helps communicate these benefits through individuals who have personally experienced studying or researching in Germany.

Purpose of the DAAD Young Ambassadors Programme

The programme aims to:

  • Promote Germany as a preferred destination for higher education.
  • Increase awareness of German universities and research institutions.
  • Encourage talented students to pursue international education.
  • Share authentic experiences from former and current students.
  • Strengthen educational cooperation between Germany and participating countries.
  • Build a network of motivated education ambassadors.
  • Inspire future applicants through peer engagement.

What Will DAAD Young Ambassadors Do?

Selected ambassadors will actively participate in promoting educational opportunities in Germany.

Typical responsibilities include:

1. Sharing Personal Experiences

Participants explain:

  • Their academic journey
  • Student life in Germany
  • Research experiences
  • Cultural experiences
  • Career development after studying in Germany

These firsthand stories help prospective students better understand what studying in Germany is truly like.

2. Conducting Presentations

Young Ambassadors organize or participate in presentations at:

  • Universities
  • Colleges
  • Schools
  • Career fairs
  • Education expos
  • Information sessions

These presentations introduce students to:

  • German universities
  • Study programmes
  • Scholarships
  • Research opportunities
  • Student life
  • Application processes

3. Participating in Educational Events

Ambassadors represent DAAD during various outreach events, including:

  • Study abroad fairs
  • Information seminars
  • Educational exhibitions
  • University outreach programmes
  • Student networking sessions

4. Inspiring Future Students

A key objective is encouraging talented students to pursue academic opportunities in Germany by providing reliable information and practical advice.

Who Can Apply?

DAAD welcomes applications from motivated individuals who meet all eligibility requirements.

Applicants must:

  • Be nationals of India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, or Sri Lanka.
  • Have studied or currently be studying or conducting research at a German institution.
  • Be below 32 years of age as of 1 January 2027.
  • Be enthusiastic about promoting Germany through educational presentations or events.
  • Be willing and able to participate in the online Young Ambassadors Training Workshop scheduled for November 2026.

Meeting all eligibility criteria is essential for consideration.

Age Requirement

Applicants must be:

  • Under 32 years of age as of 1 January 2027.

This age requirement ensures the programme engages young professionals and recent academic participants who can effectively connect with prospective students.

Previous German Study or Research Experience

Applicants must have direct academic or research experience in Germany.

Eligible individuals include those who:

  • Previously studied at a German university.
  • Are currently studying in Germany.
  • Previously conducted research in Germany.
  • Are currently conducting research at a German institution.

Having firsthand experience enables ambassadors to provide authentic guidance to prospective applicants.

Passion for Educational Outreach

Academic qualifications alone are not sufficient.

DAAD is looking for individuals who are:

  • Passionate about Germany
  • Excellent communicators
  • Motivated to inspire others
  • Comfortable speaking publicly
  • Interested in educational outreach
  • Willing to organize presentations and events

Communication skills and enthusiasm play an important role in becoming an effective ambassador.

Mandatory Training Workshop

Successful applicants must participate in the online Young Ambassadors Training Workshop scheduled for November 2026.

The training prepares ambassadors by providing guidance on:

  • Programme objectives
  • Outreach strategies
  • Presentation techniques
  • Communication skills
  • Promotional activities
  • Representing DAAD professionally

Attendance is mandatory.

Benefits of Becoming a DAAD Young Ambassador

Although this is not a scholarship programme, selected ambassadors receive valuable professional and personal development opportunities.

These include:

Leadership Development

Participants strengthen their leadership abilities through educational outreach and public engagement.

Public Speaking Experience

Ambassadors gain confidence by delivering presentations and interacting with diverse audiences.

Networking Opportunities

Participants become part of a growing network of:

  • DAAD representatives
  • German institutions
  • Education professionals
  • Fellow ambassadors
  • Students

International Exposure

The programme strengthens participants’ international profile while maintaining connections with Germany’s academic community.

Professional Recognition

Serving as a DAAD Young Ambassador demonstrates commitment to international education and community engagement, enhancing professional credentials.

Opportunity to Inspire Others

Perhaps the greatest reward is helping future students access life-changing educational opportunities in Germany.

Why Your Experience Matters

Students often trust advice from peers who have already experienced studying abroad.

By sharing practical experiences about:

  • Student life
  • Academic expectations
  • Cultural adjustment
  • Living costs
  • Research opportunities
  • Campus experiences
  • Career development

Young Ambassadors help prospective applicants make informed decisions and prepare for successful study experiences in Germany.

Application Deadline

Interested applicants must submit their applications before:

Deadline: 30 September 2026

Late applications may not be considered, so prospective ambassadors are encouraged to apply well before the closing date.

How to Apply

Eligible applicants should complete the official online application through the DAAD application portal before the deadline.

Applicants are encouraged to carefully review all eligibility requirements and prepare any necessary supporting information before submitting their applications.

APPLY HERE

Why You Should Apply

If your academic journey in Germany has positively influenced your education, career, or personal growth, becoming a DAAD Young Ambassador offers an opportunity to give back.

By joining this programme, you can:

  • Inspire future generations of students.
  • Promote international education.
  • Share valuable academic experiences.
  • Develop leadership and communication skills.
  • Expand your professional network.
  • Continue contributing to Germany’s global academic community.

For motivated young professionals and students who enjoy mentoring others, this programme represents an excellent opportunity to make a lasting educational impact.

Visit HERE for more information about the DAAD Young Ambassadors 2027 programme.

Conclusion

The DAAD Young Ambassadors 2027 Programme provides a meaningful opportunity for former and current students and researchers with German academic experience to become advocates for international education. Through presentations, outreach activities, and educational events, ambassadors play an important role in encouraging talented students to explore Germany’s outstanding universities and research institutions.

Beyond promoting study opportunities, the programme also helps participants strengthen their leadership, communication, and networking skills while remaining connected to the German academic community. If you meet the eligibility criteria and are passionate about sharing your educational journey, this is an excellent opportunity to inspire future scholars and contribute to international academic cooperation.

Remember to submit your application before the 30 September 2026 deadline to be considered for the 2027 cohort.

For more global Fellowship opportunities, visit OFY HERE.

item.content:encoded:
Women for Women International (WfWI) is inviting experienced global development leaders to apply for the position of Chief Programs & Partnerships Officer (CPPO). This permanent executive leadership role offers an exceptional opportunity to shape the future of one of the world’s leading organizations dedicated to supporting women survivors of war and conflict.

The successful candidate will join WfWI’s Executive Leadership Team and play a central role in defining the organization’s global program strategy, strengthening institutional partnerships, ensuring program quality, guiding evidence-based decision-making, and leading global business development initiatives. The position is available to professionals who already possess the legal right to work in one of the approved countries, including Ghana, Kenya, Rwanda, South Africa, Nigeria, Iraq, Germany, the United Kingdom, or the United States.

This role is ideal for highly accomplished international development professionals with extensive experience leading complex humanitarian and development programs across multiple countries, particularly within fragile and conflict-affected settings.

About Women for Women International

Women for Women International (WfWI) is a globally recognized nonprofit organization committed to empowering women who have survived war, armed conflict, and humanitarian crises.

Since its founding in 1993, the organization has supported more than 550,000 women across 17 conflict-affected countries, helping them rebuild their lives through economic empowerment, education, rights awareness, health information, and community leadership.

WfWI currently works in countries including:

  • Afghanistan
  • Bosnia and Herzegovina
  • Democratic Republic of the Congo
  • Iraq
  • Kosovo
  • Nigeria
  • Rwanda
  • South Sudan

Through its flagship Stronger Women, Stronger Nations Programme, participants gain:

  • Livelihood and vocational skills
  • Financial literacy
  • Savings and income-generation knowledge
  • Leadership development
  • Women’s rights education
  • Health awareness
  • Community support networks

The organization believes that empowering women creates stronger families, stronger communities, and ultimately more peaceful societies.

Position Overview

Position: Chief Programs & Partnerships Officer (CPPO)

Department: Global Programs Unit

Employment Type: Full-time

Contract: Permanent / Open-ended

Leadership Grade: L

Reports To: International Chief Executive Officer

Work Arrangement: Remote or Hybrid (depending on location)

Eligible Work Locations

Applicants must already have legal authorization to work in one of the following countries:

  • Ghana
  • Kenya
  • Rwanda
  • South Africa
  • Nigeria
  • Iraq
  • Germany
  • United Kingdom
  • United States

Women for Women International does not sponsor work visas and does not provide relocation support.

An Executive Leadership Role with Global Impact

The Chief Programs & Partnerships Officer serves as one of the most senior executives within Women for Women International.

As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the CPPO helps shape the organization’s future by ensuring that every program remains:

  • Mission-driven
  • Evidence-based
  • Financially sustainable
  • Operationally feasible
  • Centered on women’s needs
  • Responsive to changing humanitarian contexts

The role serves as the International CEO’s principal strategic advisor on matters involving:

  • Global program strategy
  • Organizational growth
  • Geographic expansion
  • Institutional partnerships
  • Program coherence
  • Funding alignment
  • Delivery continuity

Rather than directly managing all country offices permanently, the CPPO provides strategic oversight through a matrix leadership structure that ensures consistent program quality across regions.

Major Responsibilities

The position covers several broad leadership functions.

1. Lead Global Program Strategy

The CPPO will oversee the organization’s entire global programming approach.

Responsibilities include:

  • Leading the development of WfWI’s global program strategy
  • Ensuring all programs remain evidence-informed
  • Improving program quality worldwide
  • Designing innovative interventions
  • Maintaining global technical standards
  • Establishing quality assurance systems
  • Aligning all programming with organizational strategy

The successful candidate will ensure that every country program delivers meaningful impact while remaining operationally realistic.

2. Strengthen Program Quality Across Regions

One of the primary responsibilities is ensuring consistency throughout WfWI’s international operations.

This includes:

  • Working closely with Regional Directors
  • Supporting Country Directors
  • Monitoring delivery quality
  • Reviewing annual country plans
  • Assessing implementation risks
  • Supporting organizational transitions
  • Maintaining strong technical oversight

The CPPO will ensure that local implementation aligns with global organizational standards.

3. Guide Program Design and Innovation

The executive will oversee technical teams responsible for:

  • Program Design
  • Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning (MERL)
  • Country Office Support
  • Grant Management
  • Program Planning

Key duties include:

  • Approving new program models
  • Reviewing innovations
  • Supporting research initiatives
  • Strengthening evidence generation
  • Promoting data-driven decision-making
  • Improving operational efficiency
  • Ensuring scalability of interventions

4. Lead the Crisis Response Fund

The CPPO serves as Executive Sponsor of WfWI’s Crisis Response Fund.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Chairing the Steering Committee
  • Approving funding allocations
  • Reviewing high-risk partnerships
  • Supporting emergency interventions
  • Managing conflict-response strategies
  • Ensuring safeguarding compliance
  • Coordinating fundraising for crisis programming

This work enables WfWI to support women in countries where it may not yet maintain permanent offices.

5. Oversee Business Development

An important part of the role involves leading institutional fundraising and strategic partnerships.

Responsibilities include:

  • Guiding the Global Business Development Unit
  • Developing fundraising strategies

item.content:encoded:
Healthcare organisations and patient advocacy groups across the United Kingdom now have an opportunity to secure funding through the MSD UK 2026 Grants Programme. Following the success of its 2025 programme, MSD UK has officially opened the second application window for its 2026 grants, inviting eligible organisations to submit innovative projects that address health inequalities and improve patient and population health.

The programme reflects MSD UK’s ongoing commitment to supporting healthcare initiatives that create meaningful, measurable, and sustainable improvements in public health. By providing arm’s-length financial grants, MSD UK enables organisations to develop and implement projects that may otherwise struggle to secure funding.

If your organisation is working to improve healthcare access, reduce inequalities, strengthen community care, promote disease prevention, or leverage digital innovation for healthier communities, this funding opportunity could help bring your project to life.

About the MSD UK Grants Programme

The MSD UK Grants Programme is designed to provide financial support to eligible healthcare and patient organisations that are committed to improving health outcomes throughout the United Kingdom.

Rather than funding routine operations, the programme focuses on supporting projects that have the potential to create lasting positive change by addressing some of the UK’s most pressing healthcare challenges.

The programme specifically seeks initiatives that:

  • Reduce health inequalities.
  • Improve patient experiences and outcomes.
  • Support healthier populations.
  • Strengthen healthcare delivery.
  • Encourage innovation in healthcare services.
  • Promote sustainable public health improvements.

MSD UK believes that many impactful healthcare projects never move beyond the planning stage due to financial constraints. Through this grants programme, the organisation aims to help remove that barrier and enable meaningful community impact.

Building on the Success of the 2025 Programme

The 2025 MSD UK Grants Programme received an unprecedented number of applications, demonstrating the growing need for funding within the healthcare sector.

Highlights from the previous programme include:

  • Two application windows.
  • A record number of submissions.
  • Funding awarded to 18 impactful healthcare projects.
  • Support provided to organisations working directly with patients and local communities.

Following this success, MSD UK has expanded its commitment by launching another funding round for 2026.

Focus Areas for the 2026 Grants Programme

The 2026 programme places particular emphasis on projects that respond to evolving priorities within the UK healthcare system.

Eligible projects should address one or more of the following themes:

1. Community and Neighbourhood Care

MSD UK is interested in initiatives that strengthen healthcare delivery within local communities.

Examples include:

  • Community healthcare services
  • Local health partnerships
  • Neighbourhood-based patient support
  • Integrated care approaches
  • Community outreach programmes

Projects should demonstrate how they improve healthcare accessibility and patient experiences at the local level.

2. Prevention-Focused Healthcare

Preventing illness before it develops remains one of the most effective ways to improve population health.

MSD UK welcomes projects focused on:

  • Early disease detection
  • Health screening initiatives
  • Preventive education
  • Lifestyle interventions
  • Risk reduction programmes
  • Public awareness campaigns

Successful proposals should demonstrate how prevention can reduce healthcare burdens while improving long-term outcomes.

3. Digital Innovation for Healthy Living

Technology continues to transform healthcare delivery.

The grants programme encourages projects that use digital innovation to promote healthier behaviours and improve patient care.

Potential examples include:

  • Digital health platforms
  • Mobile health applications
  • Virtual patient education
  • Digital patient engagement tools
  • Remote monitoring initiatives
  • Technology-enabled community health services

Projects should clearly demonstrate how digital solutions can improve health outcomes or increase healthcare accessibility.

Types of Projects Eligible for Funding

The programme supports a broad range of healthcare initiatives, including:

  • Educational programmes
  • Patient awareness campaigns
  • Community health initiatives
  • Patient advocacy projects
  • Population health interventions
  • Innovative healthcare delivery models
  • Digital healthcare solutions
  • Preventive health programmes
  • Local community support initiatives

Projects should have clear objectives, measurable outcomes, and the potential for sustainable impact.

Who Can Apply?

Applications are open to eligible healthcare organisations and patient organisations operating within the United Kingdom.

These organisations should have projects that align with MSD UK’s objectives of improving patient care, reducing health inequalities, and supporting public health priorities.

Applicants are encouraged to review the full eligibility guidance before preparing their proposals.

Why This Funding Matters

Healthcare inequalities continue to affect communities throughout the UK.

Many innovative organisations have ideas capable of transforming patient care but lack sufficient financial resources to implement them.

The MSD UK Grants Programme seeks to bridge this gap by supporting projects that:

  • Improve access to healthcare.
  • Reduce disparities in health outcomes.
  • Strengthen local healthcare systems.
  • Empower patients.
  • Promote healthier lifestyles.
  • Encourage innovation within healthcare delivery.

Ultimately, the programme contributes to a stronger and more equitable healthcare system across the United Kingdom.

Funding Approach

MSD UK provides arm’s-length financial grants, ensuring an independent funding process while enabling organisations to develop impactful healthcare initiatives.

Funding is intended to support projects that deliver measurable benefits to patients and communities rather than routine organisational activities.

Click HERE to read more.

Application Process

Eligible organisations wishing to apply should:

  1. Review the programme scope and eligibility requirements.
  2. Develop a project proposal aligned with the programme priorities.
  3. Complete the online application form.
  4. Submit all required documentation before the application deadline.

Applicants are encouraged to begin preparations early to ensure sufficient time for proposal development.

Application Deadline

Eligible organisations must submit their applications by 5:00 PM on 8 September 2026.

Late applications are unlikely to be considered.

Confirmation of Application

Applicants should receive a confirmation email after submission.

If a confirmation email is not received within seven working days, organisations should contact the grants team to verify receipt of their application.

APPLY HERE

Enquiries

For questions regarding the programme or submitted applications, applicants can contact:

Email: Grantscommittee@msd.com

Additional Information

Applicants are encouraged to review MSD UK’s privacy information before submitting their applications.

Healthcare professionals should also be aware that adverse events related to medicines should be reported through the UK’s MHRA Yellow Card Scheme, alongside reporting to Merck Sharp & Dohme (UK) Limited where appropriate.

Why Organisations Should Consider Applying

The MSD UK 2026 Grants Programme represents an important funding opportunity for organisations committed to improving healthcare across the United Kingdom.

Whether developing innovative digital health solutions, expanding community-based healthcare services, supporting prevention initiatives, or advocating for patients, successful applicants will receive financial support to help transform ideas into meaningful action.

For organisations dedicated to reducing health inequalities and improving lives, this programme offers the opportunity to secure funding while contributing to a healthier and more equitable future.

Conclusion

The MSD UK 2026 Grants Programme continues MSD UK’s commitment to supporting healthcare organisations and patient groups working to improve health outcomes across the UK. By funding projects focused on community care, prevention, and digital innovation, the programme aims to create sustainable improvements that benefit both patients and wider populations.

Eligible organisations with impactful ideas are encouraged to review the programme guidance carefully and submit their applications before 5:00 PM on 8 September 2026. With healthcare inequalities remaining a major challenge, this funding provides an opportunity to turn innovative ideas into practical solutions that deliver lasting change.

Click HERE for more grant opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
Across many rural communities in Africa, sustainable development is most effective when local people are empowered to make decisions about their own future. Rather than relying solely on externally designed development programs, communities often possess the knowledge, leadership, experience, and innovative ideas needed to solve their own challenges.

Spark Microgrants is championing this approach in Malawi by supporting community-led development that places decision-making directly into the hands of local residents. Through inclusive village planning, direct village grants, leadership development, and collaboration with community-based organizations, the initiative is helping communities identify their own priorities and transform those priorities into lasting development outcomes.

The initiative is currently expanding its work across Kasungu and Zomba districts in Malawi, where it aims to reach approximately 33,000 people in 100 villages. The lessons learned from this work are also expected to contribute to broader government-led efforts to strengthen local development planning across the country.

About Spark Microgrants

Spark Microgrants is an organization dedicated to enabling communities to drive their own development through locally led decision-making and investment.

Instead of imposing development priorities from outside, Spark Microgrants believes that communities themselves are best positioned to identify their most urgent needs and design practical solutions.

Its model focuses on:

  • Inclusive village planning
  • Community leadership development
  • Direct financial support through village grants
  • Strengthening local governance
  • Building long-term community ownership
  • Encouraging participation from marginalized groups

The organization works alongside local partners to ensure development initiatives are community-owned, transparent, and sustainable.

Supporting Community-Led Development in Rural Malawi

The current initiative focuses on rural communities throughout Malawi where local residents are encouraged to become the primary architects of their own development.

Instead of outside organizations determining community priorities, residents participate in structured planning processes that allow them to:

  • Discuss local challenges
  • Identify development priorities
  • Build consensus
  • Create practical village development plans
  • Manage project implementation
  • Oversee financial resources

This participatory approach ensures that projects reflect genuine community needs rather than externally determined objectives.

Inclusive Village Planning at the Centre of Development

One of the defining features of Spark Microgrants is its emphasis on inclusive village planning.

Communities participate in structured planning sessions where everyone has the opportunity to contribute ideas regarding local development priorities.

The planning process encourages communities to think collectively about improving:

  • Livelihoods
  • Infrastructure
  • Community services
  • Local economic opportunities
  • Social wellbeing
  • Community resilience

Rather than relying on a small group of local leaders, the planning process actively encourages broad participation from across the community.

Empowering Women, Youth and Marginalized Groups

An important component of the initiative is ensuring that development planning represents the voices of all community members.

Spark Microgrants intentionally promotes participation from groups that have historically been excluded from local decision-making processes.

These include:

  • Women
  • Young people
  • Individuals traditionally excluded from leadership roles
  • Underrepresented community members

By broadening participation, communities are able to produce more inclusive development plans that reflect shared aspirations rather than the priorities of only a few individuals.

The organization also trains elected community facilitators, with half of these facilitators being women. These facilitators guide village planning discussions, encourage participation, and help communities move from planning to implementation.

Direct Village Grants for Community Priorities

After communities identify their priorities and prepare development plans, Spark Microgrants provides direct village grants that allow communities to implement their own projects.

Instead of outside agencies managing every aspect of implementation, residents themselves oversee the use of resources.

Community members are responsible for:

  1. Managing project funds.
  2. Coordinating implementation.
  3. Monitoring progress.
  4. Ensuring accountability.
  5. Maintaining completed projects.

This community ownership strengthens local accountability while building long-term leadership capacity.

Partnership with Community-Based Organizations

Spark Microgrants works closely with Malawian community-based organizations that understand local contexts and community needs.

These partnerships help ensure that:

  • Community engagement remains culturally appropriate.
  • Local knowledge informs implementation.
  • Capacity is strengthened within existing organizations.
  • Development efforts remain sustainable.

Working through local organizations also helps strengthen community institutions that will continue supporting development beyond the duration of individual projects.

Expansion Across Kasungu and Zomba

The initiative will be implemented in:

  • Kasungu District
  • Zomba District

Across these districts, Spark Microgrants plans to support:

  • 100 villages
  • Approximately 33,000 people

This represents a significant expansion of community-led development efforts designed to improve local governance and strengthen community participation.

Building Evidence for National Scale

An important objective of the initiative is not only to support current communities but also to generate evidence for future policy development.

The experience gained from implementation across the participating villages will inform an anticipated next phase involving collaboration with:

  • The Government of Malawi
  • The World Bank

The future phase is expected to explore how inclusive village planning can be integrated into district government systems, giving communities a stronger voice in shaping local development priorities.

If successful, the model could influence how community participation is incorporated into public planning processes throughout Malawi.

Community Savings and Collective Investment

Beyond planning and grants, participating communities also establish communal savings mechanisms.

These savings are collectively managed by the village and provide opportunities for communities to:

  • Build financial resilience.
  • Invest in shared priorities.
  • Support future development activities.
  • Strengthen local ownership of community assets.

Collective financial management reinforces accountability while creating long-term community investment structures.

Key Features of the Spark Microgrants Model

Some of the major components of the initiative include:

  • Community-led decision-making
  • Inclusive village planning
  • Direct village grants
  • Leadership development
  • Women’s participation in leadership
  • Youth engagement
  • Partnership with local organizations
  • Community-managed investments
  • Collective savings initiatives
  • Strengthened local governance
  • Evidence generation for national policy
  • Collaboration with government institutions

Why This Initiative Matters

Traditional development models often rely heavily on external planning and implementation.

Spark Microgrants demonstrates an alternative approach where communities:

  • Identify their own priorities.
  • Design their own solutions.
  • Manage their own resources.
  • Strengthen local leadership.
  • Build long-term ownership.

By placing decision-making in the hands of local residents, the initiative supports sustainable development that reflects the unique needs and aspirations of each community.

Its emphasis on inclusion, accountability, and local ownership also contributes to stronger governance systems and greater community resilience.

Learn More

Individuals interested in learning more about Spark Microgrants and its work can visit the organization’s official website for additional information about its community-led development approach and global initiatives.

Visit HERE for more information about the Spark Microgrants in Malawi.

Conclusion

Spark Microgrants is helping reshape rural development in Malawi by demonstrating that communities are capable of leading their own progress when provided with the necessary tools, resources, and support. Through inclusive planning, direct village grants, leadership development, and partnerships with local organizations, the initiative empowers residents to determine their own future while strengthening local governance and community ownership.

With implementation across 100 villages in Kasungu and Zomba expected to benefit approximately 33,000 people, the initiative also serves as an important learning opportunity for future collaboration with the Government of Malawi and the World Bank. If successfully integrated into district planning systems, this community-led approach has the potential to influence development practices far beyond the initial project areas, creating stronger and more inclusive pathways for local development across Malawi.

item.content:encoded:
The Estonian Centre for International Development (ESTDEV) has announced a new procurement opportunity under the Africa-Europe Digital Innovation Bridge (AEDIB) programme, inviting qualified service providers to conduct a comprehensive ecosystem mapping study of Entrepreneurship Support Organisations (ESOs) and Innovation Support Organisations (ISOs) across multiple African countries.

This procurement presents an excellent opportunity for consulting firms, research organisations, innovation ecosystem experts, policy analysts, and development consulting agencies with expertise in entrepreneurship and digital innovation. The selected service provider will lead a multi-country study aimed at strengthening the understanding of digital innovation ecosystems across Africa and identifying opportunities for greater cooperation between African and European innovation stakeholders.

With an estimated procurement value of €120,000, the project seeks to generate valuable evidence that will support policymakers, innovation hubs, entrepreneurs, investors, governments, and development partners in making informed decisions to strengthen Africa’s digital innovation landscape.

Application Deadline: 17 August 2026

About the Advanced Entrepreneurship/Innovation Support Organisations Ecosystem Mapping Procurement

The procurement has been launched by ESTDEV as part of the Africa-Europe Digital Innovation Bridge (AEDIB) initiative.

The main objective is to identify and analyze organisations that provide support to entrepreneurs and innovators throughout African countries. These organisations play an essential role in helping startups, technology companies, social enterprises, researchers, and innovators grow by offering services such as incubation, acceleration, mentoring, funding access, networking opportunities, training, business development support, and innovation programmes.

The successful bidder will conduct a detailed mapping exercise that creates a comparable overview of innovation ecosystems across several African countries.

Rather than collecting entirely new datasets, the assignment will primarily rely on reviewing and analysing existing research, reports, databases, and ecosystem studies.

Purpose of the Procurement

The primary purpose of this procurement is to strengthen understanding of digital innovation ecosystems across Africa.

The ecosystem mapping study aims to:

  • Identify organisations supporting entrepreneurship and innovation.
  • Compare innovation ecosystems across multiple African countries.
  • Examine how digital innovation ecosystems function.
  • Identify key actors involved in ecosystem development.
  • Highlight opportunities for collaboration.
  • Analyze ecosystem strengths and weaknesses.
  • Identify barriers affecting innovation growth.
  • Explore factors driving ecosystem development.
  • Support evidence-based policymaking.
  • Improve Africa-Europe cooperation in digital innovation.

The findings are expected to contribute to stronger partnerships between African and European innovation ecosystems while supporting sustainable entrepreneurship development.

Scope of the Ecosystem Mapping Study

The selected service provider will conduct a comprehensive multi-country study focusing on entrepreneurship and innovation support organisations.

The assignment will include:

  1. Review of Existing Data
    • Analyze previously published studies.
    • Examine available ecosystem reports.
    • Review existing innovation databases.
    • Consolidate available evidence.
  2. Innovation Ecosystem Mapping
    • Identify Entrepreneurship Support Organisations (ESOs).
    • Identify Innovation Support Organisations (ISOs).
    • Classify ecosystem stakeholders.
    • Compare ecosystem structures across countries.
  3. Digital Innovation Ecosystem Analysis
    • Assess ecosystem maturity.
    • Examine innovation support mechanisms.
    • Analyze collaboration models.
    • Identify ecosystem strengths and challenges.
  4. Comparative Country Analysis
    • Develop comparable country profiles.
    • Examine regional similarities and differences.
    • Highlight best practices.
    • Identify cooperation opportunities.

Objectives of the Study

The ecosystem mapping exercise seeks to achieve several important objectives, including:

  • Creating a comprehensive overview of innovation ecosystems across selected African countries.
  • Understanding the role played by Entrepreneurship Support Organisations.
  • Understanding the contribution of Innovation Support Organisations.
  • Identifying major ecosystem stakeholders.
  • Supporting digital transformation initiatives.
  • Encouraging regional collaboration.
  • Promoting stronger Africa-Europe innovation partnerships.
  • Generating evidence to inform future innovation investments and policies.

Why This Procurement Matters

Entrepreneurship and innovation ecosystems are essential drivers of economic development.

By mapping these ecosystems, the study will help stakeholders better understand:

  • Where innovation support is strongest.
  • Existing gaps in entrepreneurial support.
  • Opportunities for investment.
  • Potential regional partnerships.
  • Capacity-building needs.
  • Ecosystem development priorities.
  • Digital transformation opportunities.
  • Innovation policy improvements.

The study will provide valuable information for governments, development organisations, investors, innovation hubs, universities, accelerators, incubators, startups, and policymakers.

€120,000

  • Innovation ecosystem research

  • Public policy analysis

Introduction

The Imagine Award by the Promise Fund stands as one of the most transformative opportunities for early childhood innovators across the United States. Designed to empower community-rooted leaders, this award provides $20,000 in flexible funding and a six-month cohort-based learning experience to help changemakers turn their ideas into reality.

Since 2018, the Promise Venture Studio has been committed to equipping social innovators with the resources, relationships, and runway they need to build a more abundant and just future for young children and families. The Imagine Award continues this legacy by focusing on leaders who are deeply connected to their communities and who bring firsthand insight into the challenges faced by families.

This award is not just about financial support—it is about building capacity, fostering innovation, and strengthening leadership. Recipients will learn how to design and execute lightweight tests for rapid learning, gain clarity on their idea’s direction using impact and business models, and craft compelling stories to attract future partnerships.

The Imagine Award is a call to action for those who believe in equity, justice, and community-driven change. It invites leaders who are ready to pilot transformative ideas that can reshape early childhood experiences, ensuring that every child has access to opportunity, care, and growth.

What the Imagine Award Provides

  1. $20,000 Flexible Grant Funding
    • Funds can be used at the recipient’s discretion to pursue tests or pilots of transformative ideas.
    • Flexibility ensures leaders can adapt resources to their unique contexts.
  2. Partnership with Promise
    • Direct, one-on-one support from the Promise team.
    • Tailored help and relevant connections to strengthen pilots.
  3. In-Person Convening
    • Multi-day gatherings for peer connection, learning, and pilot design.
  4. Mentoring
    • Access to experienced mentors to guide awardees through pilot design and beyond.
  5. Cohort Workshops and Gatherings
    • Light, tailored coaching to support pilot preparation, launch, and implementation.
  6. Alumni Support
    • Ongoing peer community and resources for continued learning and collaboration.

Who the Imagine Award Funds

Awardees are expected to be:

  • Based in and primarily serving children and families in the U.S.
  • Deeply connected to communities impacted by their work.

16. How does Promise ensure equity and inclusion? Promise prioritizes leaders and ideas that center community voice, equity, and justice. The program actively seeks diversity in its cohorts.

17. What is the Promise Fund? The Promise Fund is an initiative by Promise Venture Studio that supports social innovators in early childhood through funding, mentorship, and community-building.

18. What is the selection process like? Applications are reviewed by a committee that evaluates clarity of ideas, community connection, readiness for piloting, and commitment to equity. Finalists are interviewed before the final selection.

The Imagine Award by the Promise Fund is more than a grant—it is a movement to empower community-rooted leaders who are shaping the future of early childhood development. With $20,000 in flexible funding, mentorship, and a six-month learning journey, awardees gain the tools, confidence, and connections needed to transform their ideas into impactful pilots.

This award recognizes that innovation begins at the community level. By supporting leaders who understand the lived experiences of families and children, the Promise Fund ensures that solutions are equitable, sustainable, and deeply relevant.

For those ready to take the next step in their journey as changemakers, the Imagine Award offers an unparalleled opportunity to learn, grow, and lead.

item.content:encoded:
The Scaleup Europe Fund (SEF) is a landmark multi-billion-euro investment initiative created to accelerate the growth of Europe’s most promising technology companies. Designed to strengthen Europe’s competitiveness in strategic industries, the Fund will provide substantial late-stage and growth capital to innovative businesses developing breakthrough technologies across the continent.

Backed by the European Commission and some of Europe’s largest institutional investors, the Scaleup Europe Fund aims to bridge the investment gap facing European scaleups and ensure that high-growth companies have access to the financial resources they need to expand globally while remaining rooted in Europe.

As part of the European Union Startup and Scaleup Strategy, the Fund represents one of the largest coordinated efforts to support strategic technology innovation, helping Europe compete with global innovation leaders while strengthening economic resilience and technological sovereignty.

With its first investments expected to begin in autumn 2026, the Scaleup Europe Fund is positioned to become one of Europe’s most influential investment vehicles for deep technology companies.

About the Scaleup Europe Fund

The Scaleup Europe Fund is a €5 billion late-stage and growth investment fund established to support European companies operating in strategic technology sectors.

Unlike traditional startup funding programmes that focus on early-stage ventures, the Scaleup Europe Fund specifically targets companies that have already demonstrated significant growth potential and are ready to scale internationally.

The Fund seeks to ensure that Europe’s most innovative businesses can continue expanding without relocating outside Europe in search of large-scale investment.

By mobilizing both public and private capital, the Fund creates an investment platform capable of supporting ambitious companies developing technologies that are critical to Europe’s future competitiveness.

Why the Scaleup Europe Fund Was Created

Europe has produced thousands of innovative startups over the past decade. However, many successful companies have struggled to secure the large-scale financing required for international expansion.

As a result, numerous European technology companies have sought investment abroad or relocated to other regions where growth capital is more readily available.

The Scaleup Europe Fund addresses this challenge by:

  • Increasing access to late-stage investment.
  • Supporting Europe’s technology champions.
  • Closing the funding gap between Europe and global innovation leaders.
  • Strengthening European technological sovereignty.
  • Keeping high-growth companies headquartered in Europe.
  • Encouraging long-term innovation and economic growth.

The initiative aligns with the European Union’s broader industrial and competitiveness agenda.

Purpose of the Fund

The Scaleup Europe Fund has several strategic objectives:

  • Support Europe’s fastest-growing technology companies.
  • Provide large-scale growth financing.
  • Strengthen Europe’s deep technology ecosystem.
  • Accelerate commercialization of breakthrough innovations.
  • Promote long-term economic competitiveness.
  • Encourage sustainable technological leadership.
  • Foster collaboration between public institutions and private investors.
  • Enable European innovators to expand globally while remaining based in Europe.

APPLY HERE

Strategic Technology Areas

The Fund focuses on companies developing technologies considered strategically important for Europe’s future.

Priority sectors include:

Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Supporting companies developing advanced AI systems, applications, infrastructure, and intelligent software solutions.

Quantum Technologies

Investing in innovations involving quantum computing, quantum communications, quantum sensing, and related technologies.

Semiconductor Technologies

Supporting companies advancing semiconductor design, manufacturing, materials, and supply chain resilience.

Robotics and Autonomous Systems

Funding innovations in robotics, automation, autonomous mobility, intelligent manufacturing, and industrial automation.

Energy Technologies

Supporting technologies that accelerate clean energy generation, storage, efficiency, and sustainable energy systems.

Space Technologies

Investing in companies developing satellite technologies, launch systems, Earth observation, space infrastructure, and related innovations.

Biotechnology

Supporting breakthrough biological innovations across healthcare, agriculture, and industrial biotechnology.

Medical Technologies

Funding companies developing advanced healthcare technologies, diagnostics, digital health, and medical devices.

Advanced Materials

Supporting innovations in next-generation materials with applications across multiple industries.

Agritech

Investing in technologies that improve agricultural productivity, sustainability, food systems, and climate resilience.

Geographic Scope

The Scaleup Europe Fund supports eligible companies located across:

  • European Union Member States.
  • All regions of Europe participating within the programme framework.

The Fund aims to ensure broad geographic representation rather than concentrating investment in only a few innovation hubs.

Public-Private Partnership

One of the defining characteristics of the Scaleup Europe Fund is its strong collaboration between public institutions and private investors.

The Fund combines:

  • Public investment leadership.
  • Private sector expertise.
  • Institutional investment capital.
  • Market-based investment management.

This structure is intended to maximize commercial performance while supporting strategic European priorities.

Founding Investors

The Fund is supported by an impressive group of founding investors alongside the European Commission.

These include:

  • Novo Holdings
  • EIFO (Export and Investment Fund of Denmark)
  • CriteriaCaixa
  • Santander / Mouro Capital
  • Fondazione Compagnia San Paolo
  • Intesa Sanpaolo
  • Fondazione Cariplo
  • APG Asset Management (acting on behalf of Dutch pension fund ABP)
  • Wallenberg Investments
  • Allianz

These organizations collectively contribute significant investment expertise and financial capacity to the Fund.

Relationship with the European Innovation Council (EIC)

The Scaleup Europe Fund will operate:

  • Under the existing European Innovation Council (EIC) Fund umbrella structure.

However, the Fund will be managed through:

  • A fully privately owned.
  • Market-based fund management structure.

This governance model combines the strategic vision of European institutions with professional investment management.

Part of the EU Startup and Scaleup Strategy

The Scaleup Europe Fund is one of the flagship initiatives announced under the EU Startup and Scaleup Strategy.

The initiative was introduced by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen during the 2025 State of the Union Address.

Its vision is simple:

Enable Europe’s most innovative companies to choose Europe as the best place to build, scale, and compete globally.

Fund Manager Selection

Following a competitive international selection process, the European Innovation Council (EIC) Fund Board selected:

EQT

to serve as the preferred:

  • Investment adviser.
  • Fund manager.

EQT was selected after a rigorous evaluation process designed to identify the most qualified organization to manage the Fund’s investments.

Why EQT Was Selected

The selection process emphasized:

  • Investment expertise.
  • Experience managing large-scale growth funds.
  • Knowledge of deep technology investments.
  • Ability to operate independently.
  • Strong governance capabilities.

EQT will oversee investment decisions while maintaining market-based investment practices.

Next Steps

Before investment activities begin, several important milestones remain.

These include:

Finalizing Legal Agreements

EQT and the EIC Fund are currently completing legal documentation covering:

  • Fund structure.
  • Governance.
  • Investment framework.
  • Operational arrangements.

Investor Commitments

Founding investors are completing:

  • Internal due diligence.
  • Board approvals.
  • Formal investment commitments.

These processes are expected to conclude within the coming weeks.

Official Launch

The Scaleup Europe Fund and its management team will be formally presented during:

EIC Summit

Date: 3 June 2026

First Investments

The Fund is expected to begin making investments in:

Autumn 2026

Companies Eligible for Investment

The Fund targets:

  • High-growth European technology companies.
  • Late-stage startups.
  • Scaleups.
  • Strategic technology innovators.

Companies should demonstrate:

  • Strong innovation potential.
  • Significant growth prospects.
  • Strategic importance.
  • Ability to scale internationally.

Detailed investment eligibility criteria are expected to be released by the Fund manager as operations commence.

Benefits of the Scaleup Europe Fund

Eligible companies may benefit from:

  • Large-scale growth capital.
  • Access to long-term strategic investors.
  • Increased ability to scale internationally.
  • Enhanced competitiveness.
  • Support for deep technology commercialization.
  • Strong public-private investment ecosystem.
  • Improved access to experienced investment professionals.
  • Greater opportunities to remain headquartered in Europe.

Why This Fund Matters

The Scaleup Europe Fund represents a major shift in Europe’s approach to innovation financing.

Rather than allowing promising companies to seek capital elsewhere, Europe is building an investment ecosystem capable of supporting technology leaders throughout their growth journey.

The Fund is expected to strengthen Europe’s position in advanced technologies while encouraging long-term innovation, job creation, industrial resilience, and sustainable economic growth.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Scaleup Europe Fund 2026

Conclusion

The Scaleup Europe Fund marks a transformative step in Europe’s innovation ecosystem by creating a dedicated €5 billion investment vehicle for high-growth technology companies operating in strategic sectors. Through strong collaboration between the European Commission, leading institutional investors, and professional fund management, the initiative aims to close Europe’s scaleup funding gap and empower innovative companies to compete globally.

With investment activity expected to begin in autumn 2026, the Fund offers significant opportunities for Europe’s most promising deep tech businesses to secure the capital needed for international expansion while contributing to Europe’s technological leadership. Eligible companies should closely monitor updates from the Fund as application and investment engagement processes become available.
