item.content:encoded:
Introduction

The Permanent Mission of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to the United Nations in Geneva is inviting applications for the position of Human Rights Policy Officer within its Political Affairs Section. This opportunity offers a chance to contribute to the Netherlands’ proactive and visible role in global human rights diplomacy at the United Nations’ hub in Geneva.

Geneva stands as the global center for human rights, hosting the Human Rights Council (HRC) and numerous international organizations. The Netherlands, a committed member of the HRC until the end of 2026, has consistently demonstrated leadership in negotiations on both thematic and country-specific human rights issues. Guided by the Human Rights, Democracy and International Rule of Law (MDIR) policy framework, the Netherlands’ engagement in Geneva reflects its dedication to advancing human rights, democracy, and the rule of law worldwide.

This position is ideal for professionals with a strong background in international law, human rights, or international relations, and experience working in multilateral environments. The successful candidate will join a small, dynamic team of diplomats and policy officers, contributing to the Netherlands’ influential presence in the Human Rights Council and related UN processes.

Position Details

  • Title: Human Rights Policy Officer
  • Department: Political Affairs Section
  • Location: Permanent Mission of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to the United Nations, Geneva
  • Contract Duration: 1 September 2026 – 31 December 2026
  • Employment Type: Full-time (1 FTE, 40 hours per week)
  • Salary Scale: Scale 10 (under the Terms and Conditions of Employment for Locally Engaged Staff of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

Job Description

The Human Rights Policy Officer will play a key role in supporting the Netherlands’ engagement with the Human Rights Council (HRC) and related UN bodies. The position involves substantive policy work, coordination, and representation in multilateral settings.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Policy Development and Analysis
    • Contribute to the Netherlands’ human rights agenda in Geneva.
    • Analyze thematic and country-specific human rights issues.
    • Prepare policy briefs, reports, and recommendations for the Mission’s leadership.
  2. Representation and Negotiation
    • Support Dutch participation in HRC sessions and related meetings.
    • Engage with counterparts from other diplomatic missions, UN agencies, and NGOs.
    • Assist in negotiations and drafting of resolutions and statements.
  3. Coordination and Liaison
    • Maintain close collaboration with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in The Hague.
    • Coordinate with other Dutch diplomatic missions and relevant departments.
    • Facilitate communication between the Mission and external stakeholders.
  4. Research and Reporting
    • Monitor developments in human rights discussions and country situations.
    • Prepare analytical reports and summaries for internal and external use.
  5. Team Collaboration
    • Work closely with colleagues in the Political Affairs Section and across the Mission.
    • Contribute to a collegial, flexible, and proactive team environment.

Candidate Profile

The successful candidate will possess a strong academic and professional background, along with the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, multilateral environment.

Required Qualifications

  • Academic degree in international law, human rights, or international relations.
  • Professional experience with multilateral organizations, preferably in the field of human rights.
  • Excellent command of Dutch and English, both written and spoken.
  • Outstanding drafting and communication skills.
  • Strong political awareness, cultural sensitivity, and networking abilities.
  • Proven organizational skills and ability to manage multiple tasks under pressure.

Desirable Qualifications

  • Knowledge of French (considered an asset).
  • Experience working in Geneva or within the UN system.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and collaboratively in diverse teams.

Working Environment

The Permanent Mission of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to the United Nations in Geneva comprises approximately 18 diplomatic staff and 9 locally recruited employees. The Mission operates through three policy sections—Political Affairs, Economic Affairs, and the Disarmament Delegation—which collaborate closely on cross-cutting issues.

Human rights are a central priority for the Mission, reflected in its active participation in the Human Rights Council, Universal Periodic Review (UPR) process, and other UN mechanisms. The Netherlands’ approach is characterized by proactivity, visibility, and collaboration, ensuring its voice is heard in key global discussions.

Working days are often long, and the workload is high, particularly during HRC sessions and UPR reviews. However, the Mission maintains a flat organizational structure and a collegial atmosphere, fostering teamwork and mutual support.

The Human Rights Policy Officer will interact regularly with:

  • UN bodies such as the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR)
  • International NGOs and civil society organizations
  • Other diplomatic missions, including those beyond the European Union
  • Dutch government departments and foreign missions

Required Competencies

Candidates should demonstrate the following core competencies:

  1. Analytical Thinking – Ability to assess complex political and human rights issues.
  2. Communication Skills – Excellent written and oral communication in Dutch and English.
  3. Negotiation Skills – Capacity to represent and advocate effectively in multilateral settings.
  4. Teamwork – Commitment to collaboration and collegiality.
  5. Initiative – Proactive approach to problem-solving and project management.
  6. Networking – Strong interpersonal skills and ability to build professional relationships.

Diversity and Inclusion

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs actively promotes diversity and inclusion within its workforce. The Netherlands values the unique perspectives and experiences that diverse teams bring to diplomacy and policymaking.

Applicants are encouraged to highlight in their motivation letter how they would contribute to the Mission’s diversity objectives, including aspects such as age, sexual orientation, gender identity, cultural background, experience, and competencies.

Terms of Employment

  • Employment governed by the Terms and Conditions of Employment for Locally Engaged Staff of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
  • Classified under salary scale 10.
  • Local employment contract with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Application Procedure

Interested candidates are invited to submit:

  1. A motivation letter explaining their interest and suitability for the position.
  2. A curriculum vitae (CV) detailing relevant qualifications and experience.

Applications should be sent via email to GEV-HR@minbuza.nl by 14 August 2026.

The recruitment process will include one or more interviews. The vacancy is open to both internal and external candidates.

For further information about the position, applicants may contact the Mission through the same email address.

 

For further application details, click HERE and apply today!

Deadline

Application Deadline: 14 August 2026

1. What is the duration of the contract? The contract runs from 1 September 2026 to 31 December 2026, making it a four-month full-time engagement.

2. Is this position full-time or part-time? It is a full-time role (1 FTE, 40 hours per week).

3. Where is the position based? The position is based at the Permanent Mission of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to the United Nations in Geneva.

4. Is this an entry-level position? No. This is not an entry-level role. Candidates must have prior knowledge and professional experience in multilateral environments, preferably in human rights.

5. What academic background is required? Applicants should hold an academic degree, preferably in international law, human rights, or international relations.

6. What professional experience is expected? Candidates should have demonstrable experience working with multilateral organizations, ideally in the field of human rights. Experience in Geneva or within the UN system is highly valued.

7. What languages are required?

  • Dutch and English: Excellent written and spoken command is mandatory.
  • French: Not essential, but considered an asset.

8. What are the main responsibilities of the Human Rights Policy Officer?

  • Policy analysis and development
  • Representation in negotiations and meetings
  • Coordination with Dutch ministries and missions
  • Monitoring human rights developments
  • Drafting reports, briefs, and recommendations

9. Who will the officer work with? The officer will collaborate with:

  • Colleagues in the Political Affairs Section
  • Staff across the Mission’s three policy sections
  • Counterparts from other diplomatic missions
  • UN agencies such as OHCHR
  • International NGOs and civil society organizations
  • Dutch government departments and foreign missions

10. What is the working environment like? The Mission has a flat organizational structure and a collegial atmosphere. Workdays are long and workloads are high, especially during Human Rights Council sessions and UPR reviews.

11. What competencies are required?

  • Analytical thinking
  • Excellent communication skills
  • Negotiation skills
  • Teamwork and collegiality
  • Initiative and proactive attitude
  • Networking and relationship-building

12. How does diversity factor into recruitment? The Ministry of Foreign Affairs pursues an active diversity policy. Applicants are encouraged to explain in their motivation letter how they would contribute to diversity in terms of age, sexual orientation, gender identity, cultural background, and experience.

13. What is the salary scale? The position is classified under salary scale 10, governed by the Terms and Conditions of Employment for Locally Engaged Staff of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

14. What is the application deadline? Applications must be submitted by 14 August 2026.

15. How should applications be submitted? Candidates should send a motivation letter and curriculum vitae (CV) to GEV-HR@minbuza.nl.

16. What does the recruitment process involve? The process will consist of one or more interviews.

17. Is the vacancy open to both internal and external candidates? Yes, the vacancy is published simultaneously for internal and external applicants.

18. What is the Netherlands’ role in the Human Rights Council? The Netherlands is a member of the HRC until the end of 2026 and plays a leading role in negotiations on thematic and country-specific human rights issues.

19. What is the Universal Periodic Review (UPR)? The UPR is a process where all UN Member States are reviewed on their human rights record. It takes place three times a year and is a priority for the Netherlands.

20. What qualities will make a candidate stand out?

  • Strong drafting and analytical skills
  • Ability to work under pressure in a multilateral environment
  • Proactive and entrepreneurial mindset
  • Cultural sensitivity and political awareness
  • Demonstrated commitment to human rights

21. Is relocation support provided? As this is a locally recruited position, relocation support is not specified. Candidates should be eligible to work locally in Geneva.

22. What is the Netherlands’ broader human rights agenda? It is guided by the Human Rights, Democracy and International Rule of Law (MDIR) policy framework, emphasizing proactive engagement and leadership in multilateral negotiations.

23. How many staff members are at the Mission? The Mission consists of approximately 18 diplomatic staff and 9 locally recruited employees.

24. What is the workload like during HRC sessions? Workload is consistently high, with long working days during the three regular HRC sessions each year, which last four to six weeks.

25. How does the Mission collaborate internally? The Mission’s three policy sections—Political Affairs, Economic Affairs, and Disarmament—work closely together, ensuring cross-cutting collaboration on issues like human rights and responsible business conduct.

To lean more about the Human Rights Policy Officer Job at the Permanent Mission of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to the UN in Geneva, click HERE.

Conclusion

The Human Rights Policy Officer position at the Permanent Mission of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to the United Nations in Geneva offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the Netherlands’ leadership in global human rights diplomacy.

This role is suited for professionals who are passionate about advancing human rights, democracy, and international law through multilateral engagement. Working in Geneva—the epicenter of global human rights—provides exposure to high-level negotiations, international collaboration, and meaningful policy impact.

With its commitment to diversity, collegiality, and proactive diplomacy, the Netherlands offers an enriching environment for professionals seeking to make a tangible difference in the world.

Applicants are encouraged to apply before 14 August 2026 to join a team dedicated to solving global challenges together.

 

To explore and learn more about other job opportunities, visit the OFY page HERE.
